Apple announced the expansion of its Supplier Employee Development Fund, a $50 million education programme aimed at providing training to workers across its supply chain, with the latest addition being a brand-new Apple education centre in Vietnam.

As Apple gradually diversifies its operations and reduces its reliance on China, the country is emerging as an increasingly important manufacturing hub. The centre is operated in partnership with Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST)……

Apple first launched the Supplier Employee Development Fund in 2022, amid growing external concern over the well-being of workers in its supply chain. The company pledged $50 million and said the fund would address both worker education and respect for worker rights.

The fund's previous focus in Vietnam has been on providing training opportunities for people with disabilities, and this latest development appears to echo a programme rolled out in India earlier this year.

Apple said the programme has so far delivered 9 million training sessions globally, with a separate 108,000 supply chain employees participating in a Swift coding course.
